ingredients: 2 tbsp glutinous rice flour mixed with 250 ml water
8 garlic cloves and 20 g ginger, minced
4 green onions, cut into 4 cm lengths

Cook the rice flour and water over medium heat, stirring, for 3-4 minutes until it thickens into a translucent paste, then cool completely.
Mix the paste with gochugaru, fish sauce, saeujeot, garlic, ginger and sugar, then fold in the radish and green onions.

Add fish sauce, saeujeot, garlic, ginger and green onions and mix well with gloved hands.

8 garlic cloves and 15 g ginger, minced

Salt the radishes and greens for 1-1.5 hours, turning halfway, until the greens are limp; rinse twice and drain.
Simmer the rice flour and water over medium heat for 3 minutes into a thin paste and cool.
Mix the paste with gochugaru, fish sauce, saeujeot, garlic, ginger and sugar, then coat the radishes, greens and green onions.

Stir gochugaru, fish sauce, garlic, ginger, onion, chilies and green onion into the cooled porridge.

ingredients: 2 blocks dried fermented soybean bricks (meju), about 2 kg, from a Korean grocer

Dissolve the salt in the water to make a brine (an egg should float with a coin-sized patch showing), place the meju in a clean onggi jar, and pour the brine over.
Float the chilies, charcoal and jujubes on top, cover with mesh, and leave in a sunny spot for 40–60 days.
Lift out the soft meju and mash it with a little of the liquid; the mash is doenjang and the liquid is boiled to become soup soy sauce (guk-ganjang).
Pack the doenjang into a jar, cover with salt and age 2 months or more before using in doenjang-jjigae and ssamjang; store-bought doenjang is a fine substitute.

150 g flat fish cakes (eomuk), cut into triangles

Bring the stock to a boil in a wide shallow pan and stir in the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce and sugar.

steps: Simmer the anchovies, kelp and radish in the water for 20 minutes, then remove the anchovies and kelp.

ingredients: 2 m cleaned pork casing (intestine), rinsed well inside and out
100 g sweet potato starch noodles (dangmyeon), soaked and chopped
250 ml fresh pork blood, from a butcher
150 g bean sprouts and napa cabbage, blanched and finely chopped
2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp salt and 1 tsp black pepper
1 tbsp minced garlic and 1 tbsp ginger
steps: Mix the noodles, rice, vegetables, scallions, garlic, ginger, seasonings and perilla powder, then stir in the blood to make a loose filling.
Tie one end of the casing, fill it loosely through a funnel (no more than three-quarters full so it does not burst), and tie off into 30 cm links.
Prick a few holes, then simmer gently (not boiling) in water for 20 minutes, and steam for 25–30 minutes until firm and an inserted thermometer reads 75°C.
Slice into rounds and serve hot with salt mixed with gochugaru and pepper, steamed liver and lung, or in tteokbokki sauce.

120 g plain flour plus 30 g potato starch

Whisk the flour, starch, salt and cold sparkling water briefly into a lumpy batter.

ingredients: 40 g chopped walnuts, peanuts or mixed seeds
steps: Mix the flours, yeast, sugar, salt and lukewarm milk into a sticky dough; cover and let rise 1 hour until doubled.
Mix the brown sugar, cinnamon and nuts for the filling.
With oiled hands, take a ball of dough, flatten it, put 1 tbsp filling in the centre, and pinch closed.
Fry seam-side down in oil over medium heat for 1 minute, flip, press flat with a hotteok press or oiled spatula, and cook 2–3 minutes per side until golden and the sugar has melted.

1 tsp vegetable oil, for the moulds

Whisk the flour, baking powder, sugar, salt, 1 egg, milk and butter into a thick batter and fill each mould halfway.
Crack a whole egg on top of each, sprinkle with parsley and a pinch of salt.
Bake for 15–18 minutes until the bread is golden and the egg white is fully set; serve warm as a winter street snack.

ingredients: 600 g boneless chicken thighs, cut into 3 cm pieces
4 thick scallions (daepa), cut into 3 cm lengths
1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp rice wine and pinch pepper, for marinade
1 tbsp soy sauce and 1 clove garlic, minced
steps: Marinate the chicken in soy sauce, rice wine and pepper for 20 minutes; soak wooden skewers in water.
Thread chicken and scallion pieces alternately onto the skewers.
Grill or pan-fry in oil over medium heat for 10–12 minutes, turning, until the juices run clear and the chicken is cooked through.

1 medium potato, diced into 5 mm cubes and par-boiled (optional)
1 litre vegetable oil, for frying; sugar, ketchup and mustard to serve
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt, egg and milk into a thick, sticky batter and let rise 1 hour.
Thread a half sausage and a piece of mozzarella onto each chopstick or skewer.
Pour the batter into a tall glass, dip and twirl each skewer to coat, roll in the potato cubes if using, then in panko.
Fry at 170°C for 3–4 minutes, turning, until deep golden and the cheese has melted.
Roll in sugar and drizzle with ketchup and mustard; serve hot.

ingredients: 4 Korean sweet potatoes (goguma, purple skin and yellow flesh), about 800 g

steps: Melt the sugar in a ladle or small pan over low heat, stirring with a chopstick, for 1–2 minutes until it turns clear amber.

2 tbsp roasted soybean powder (injeolmi-garu or kinako)

Shave the frozen milk or ice finely with a shaved-ice machine or blender into a fluffy mound.
Top with the red beans, rice cakes, soybean powder and fruit.
Drizzle with condensed milk and serve at once, mixing everything together as you eat.

60 g toasted sesame seeds, ground coarsely
300 g fresh pine needles, rinsed (or a cloth-lined steamer)

Mix the sesame seeds with honey and sugar for the filling.
Roll walnut-sized pieces into balls, press a well with your thumb, add 1/2 tsp filling, seal, and shape into half-moons.
Layer on pine needles in a steamer and steam over boiling water for 20–25 minutes until glossy and cooked through.
Rinse briefly in cold water, toss with sesame oil, and serve for Chuseok.

steps: Mix the rice flour, salt, sugar and water into a smooth batter in a microwave-safe bowl.
Cover and microwave on high for 2 minutes, stir, then 2 minutes more, stir, and 1–2 minutes until translucent and very sticky (or steam 20 minutes in a cloth-lined steamer).
Pound and fold the hot dough with a wet wooden spoon for 2 minutes to make it chewy.
Turn onto a tray thickly dusted with soybean powder, dust the top, flatten to 2 cm, and cut into bite-size pieces with a scraper; roll each in more powder and serve the same day.

Spoon loosely into a cloth-lined round steamer basket, level the top without pressing, and score into portions with a knife.

1 tsp salt for the rice flour

Rub the rice flour with salt and water, sieve it, and mix in the sugar.
In a cloth-lined steamer, spread a layer of red beans, then a layer of rice flour, and repeat to finish with beans.
Steam over boiling water for 25–30 minutes until the rice layers are cooked and firm; cool slightly and slice, traditionally for moving house or gosa rituals.

3 tbsp soju or water, for the dough

Pound the hot dough until stretchy, roll 3 mm thick, cut into 1 x 4 cm strips, and dry in a warm place for 1–2 days until hard.
Soak the dried strips in 100°C oil for 1 minute, then move to 160°C oil and press gently as they puff up 3–4 times in size.

500 g sugar, or half sugar and half honey

Halve, remove seeds, and slice the peel and flesh into very thin strips.

ingredients: 1 Asian pear, thinly sliced into flower shapes

ingredients: 750 ml bottle makgeolli, bought from a licensed brewery or shop
1 plate haemul pajeon or bindaetteok, to serve
steps: Makgeolli is Korea's oldest alcoholic drink, a milky, lightly fizzy, slightly sweet-tart unfiltered rice wine of about 6–8% alcohol, made by licensed brewers from rice and nuruk starter; buy it from licensed producers rather than making it at home.
Keep it chilled, then gently tilt the bottle up and down a few times to mix the settled sediment in before opening, as it can be fizzy.

ingredients: 200 g beef sirloin, half minced and half thinly sliced
150 g firm white fish fillet (cod or pollock), sliced and dusted with flour
4 eggs, separated into yolks and whites
8 peeled walnuts and 2 tbsp pine nuts (jat)
6 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and sliced
1 small bunch minari (water dropwort) or watercress
1 small carrot, cut into thin strips
1.2 l beef brisket broth, seasoned with 1 tbsp guk-ganjang (soup soy sauce)
2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp sesame oil, 2 cloves garlic minced, 1 tsp sugar
3 tbsp vegetable oil and plain flour for dredging
steps: Season the minced beef with half the soy sauce, garlic, sugar and sesame oil, roll into small meatballs, dredge in flour and egg, and pan-fry over medium heat until browned and cooked through, about 6 minutes.

Dip the fish slices in flour and beaten egg and fry 2 minutes per side; fry the yolks and whites separately as thin sheets (jidan) over low heat, then cut everything, including blanched minari, into strips the length of the pot.

Arrange the fish, egg sheets, minari, carrot and shiitake in alternating colour wedges on top, then scatter over the meatballs, walnuts and pine nuts.
Pour in the hot broth, bring to a simmer over medium heat (or light the charcoal chimney) and cook for 10 minutes until the beef is cooked through; serve at the table with rice.

150 g beef sirloin, cut into thin strips
4 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and julienned
30 g dried seogi (stone ear mushroom) or wood ear, soaked and shredded
2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp sesame oil, 1 tsp sugar, 1 clove garlic minced
3 tbsp vegetable oil and 2 tbsp mustard sauce (gyeojajang) for dipping
steps: Whisk the flour, water and salt into a thin batter, rest 20 minutes, then spoon small 7 cm circles into a lightly oiled pan over low heat and cook 30 seconds per side without browning.
Fry the yolks and whites separately into thin egg sheets over low heat and cut into fine strips.

Stack the crepes in the centre of an octagonal gujeolpan tray and arrange the eight fillings in the outer sections; diners wrap a little of each in a crepe and dip it in mustard sauce.

ingredients: 400 g cheongpo-muk (white mung bean jelly), cut into thin batons
100 g beef sirloin, cut into thin strips
1 small bunch minari (water dropwort) or watercress, cut 4 cm long
1 egg, separated and fried into thin sheets
1 sheet gim (roasted laver), toasted and crumbled

1 tbsp sesame oil and 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds

1 small Korean pear (bae) or crisp pear, julienned
1 egg, separated and fried into thin sheets
2 tbsp Korean mustard powder (gyeoja) or Dijon mustard, 2 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tbsp sugar

4 fresh shiitake mushrooms, cut into strips
1 carrot, cut into 1 x 7 cm batons

2 eggs, made into a thick omelette and cut into batons
3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp sesame oil

1 tbsp sesame oil and 1 tsp ground black pepper

Mix the soy sauce, sugar, pear, garlic, spring onion, sesame oil and pepper, coat the beef and marinate for 30 minutes.

150 g beef sirloin, cut into strips
4 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and sliced
4 tbsp soy sauce, 1.5 tbsp sugar, 2 cloves garlic minced

1 tbsp sesame oil and 1 tbsp pine nuts, chopped

1/2 cucumber, finely chopped, salted and squeezed

1 small zucchini, julienned, salted and squeezed
3 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and finely chopped
1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1 clove garlic minced
8 fresh ivy or perilla leaves for steaming
steps: Knead the flour, water and salt into a firm dough, cover and rest 30 minutes.
Stir-fry the beef with the shiitake, garlic, soy sauce and sesame oil until cooked through, then mix with the zucchini and cool.

ingredients: 200 g plain flour, 100 ml water and 1/2 tsp salt
1 small zucchini, julienned, salted and squeezed
4 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and chopped
100 g mung bean sprouts, blanched and chopped
1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1 clove garlic minced
1 l chilled beef broth (yangji broth) seasoned with 1 tsp guk-ganjang
steps: Make a firm dough with the flour, water and salt and rest it 30 minutes.
Stir-fry the beef, shiitake and garlic with soy sauce and sesame oil until cooked, then mix with zucchini and sprouts and cool.
Roll the dough thin and cut into 8 cm squares, place filling in the centre and bring the four corners together, pinching the seams into a square pillow.

ingredients: 80 g beef sirloin, cut into fine strips
2 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and julienned
1 egg, yolk fried into a thin sheet and cut into strips
1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp sesame oil
3 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tbsp sugar and 1 tsp salt for the dressing
steps: Cut the cucumbers into 4 cm pieces and make three deep slits along each, stopping 1 cm from the ends; rub with salt and leave 15 minutes, then rinse and squeeze lightly.
Season the beef and shiitake with the soy sauce, sugar and sesame oil and stir-fry over high heat for 2–3 minutes until fully cooked.

ingredients: 80 g beef sirloin, cut into fine strips
2 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and julienned
1 egg, separated and fried into thin sheets
1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1 clove garlic minced
200 ml beef broth seasoned with 1 tsp guk-ganjang
steps: Cut the zucchini into 4 cm pieces, halve lengthways and cut three slits in each half; salt for 15 minutes and pat dry.
Stir-fry the beef and shiitake with the soy sauce, sugar, garlic and sesame oil until cooked through.
Stuff the slits with beef, mushroom and egg strips.
Place in a shallow pan with the broth, cover and simmer over medium-low heat for 5–6 minutes until the zucchini is just tender; serve with soy-vinegar sauce.

ingredients: 100 g chicken breast or beef mince
2 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and finely chopped
1 egg yolk, fried into a thin sheet and cut into strips
1 red chilli, seeded and cut into fine threads (silgochu)
1 tsp salt, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1 clove garlic minced
steps: Wrap the tofu in a cloth, squeeze out the water and mash finely.
Mix the tofu with the minced meat, shiitake, garlic, salt, sesame oil and cornstarch into a smooth paste.

Press into a 2 cm-thick square on a damp cloth in a steamer, decorate the top with egg strips, chilli threads and pine nuts, and steam over boiling water for 15 minutes until the meat is fully cooked.
Cool slightly, cut into 3 cm squares and serve with soy-vinegar dipping sauce.

ingredients: 300 g Korean radish (mu), cut into 2 cm squares
300 g napa cabbage hearts, cut into 2 cm squares
100 ml soy sauce (for salting and seasoning)
1 Korean pear, cut into 2 cm squares
4 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and sliced
3 chestnuts, sliced, and 1 tbsp pine nuts
1 small bunch minari or watercress, cut 3 cm long
3 cloves garlic and 1 thumb ginger, julienned
steps: Toss the radish and cabbage with 60 ml soy sauce and leave for 30 minutes, turning, until slightly softened; reserve the soy liquid.
Mix the vegetables with the pear, shiitake, chestnuts, garlic, ginger and minari and pack into a clean jar.
Combine the water, reserved soy liquid, remaining soy sauce and sugar and pour over to cover.
Leave at room temperature for 1 day to ferment lightly, then refrigerate; serve chilled with the broth, scattered with pine nuts, as a royal New Year side.

ingredients: 600 g lean beef top round, trimmed of all fat
1 tbsp sesame oil and 1 tbsp pine nuts, chopped
steps: Partially freeze the beef for 1 hour and slice with the grain into 4 mm sheets.
Mix the soy sauce, sugar, pear, garlic and pepper, massage into the beef and marinate in the fridge overnight.

Lay the slices flat on racks and dry in an oven at 75°C with the door slightly ajar (or a dehydrator at 70°C) for 3 hours until dry but still pliable, first making sure the meat reaches a safe temperature.
Brush with sesame oil and honey, sprinkle with chopped pine nuts, cut into squares and store airtight.

steps: Drain the rice and blend with the water until finely ground but slightly gritty.
Cook the rice slurry in a heavy pot over medium heat, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon, for 8–10 minutes until thick.
Gradually add the milk while stirring and simmer over low heat for 8 minutes until smooth and creamy, taking care it does not catch.
Season with salt, serve warm in small bowls with sugar or honey on the side and a few pine nuts, as the royal court ate it in the morning.

steps: Blend the drained rice with 400 ml water until smooth and strain; separately blend the pine nuts with 300 ml water until creamy and strain.
Bring the rice liquid and remaining 300 ml water to a simmer in a heavy pot, stirring constantly, and cook for 10 minutes until thickened.
Add the pine nut liquid little by little while stirring and cook gently for 5 minutes more without stirring too hard, so it does not split.
Season with salt at the table (salting early thins the porridge) and serve with honey and a few whole pine nuts.

ingredients: Salt and black pepper to season at the table
steps: Soak the bones in cold water overnight, changing the water a few times to draw out blood.
Blanch the bones in boiling water for 10 minutes, drain, rinse and return to a pot with 5 l fresh water; boil hard for 6–8 hours, topping up water, until milky white.
Add the brisket, onion and leek for the last 2 hours; remove the brisket when tender, cool and slice thinly.
Skim the fat, then ladle the white broth over a few noodles, rice and sliced brisket in each bowl.
Let each diner season with salt, pepper and chopped spring onion, and serve with kkakdugi and rice.

ingredients: 1.5 kg ox knee cartilage and tendon (dogani)
Salt, black pepper, and soy-wasabi dip to serve
steps: Soak the knee and shank in cold water overnight, then blanch for 10 minutes and rinse.
Simmer with 4 l water, onion, leek and garlic over low heat for 5–6 hours until the tendon is gelatinous and soft.
Lift out the meat and tendon, cut into bite-size pieces, and skim fat from the broth.
Season the broth with soup soy sauce and salt, return the meat, heat through and serve with spring onion, rice and soy-mustard or soy-wasabi dip for the tendon.

ingredients: 500 g live loach (mikkuraji), purged in salt
200 g beef tripe or offal, cleaned (optional)
3 spring onions and 1 tsp sancho (Korean pepper) powder
steps: Simmer the brisket and tripe in 3 l water for 1 hour until tender, then slice and keep the broth.
Rinse the loach well after salting, add whole to the broth (the Seoul style keeps them whole rather than ground) and simmer for 20 minutes until fully cooked.
Add the shiitake, tofu, gochugaru, garlic, soy sauce and sliced meat and simmer 10 minutes more.

ingredients: 600 g beef ribeye or sirloin, very thinly sliced
2 tbsp sugar and 3 tbsp grated Korean pear
4 fresh shiitake or enoki mushrooms, sliced
50 g dangmyeon (sweet potato glass noodles), soaked
1 tbsp sesame oil and black pepper
steps: Marinate the beef with the soy sauce, sugar, pear, garlic, sesame oil and pepper for 30 minutes.
Place the beef, onion and mushrooms around the dome of a bulgogi pan (or in a wide shallow pan) with the glass noodles in the moat.
Pour the broth into the moat and cook over medium-high heat for 8–10 minutes, stirring, until the beef is cooked through and the noodles are soft.
Add spring onions and serve the meat and broth over rice, Seoul-style with plenty of juice.

ingredients: 600 g fresh or 400 g dried buckwheat-rich naengmyeon noodles
Vinegar and Korean mustard to serve
steps: Simmer the beef with the onion and leek in 3 l water for 2 hours until tender; remove the beef, slice thinly and chill.
Strain and skim the broth, season with soup soy sauce and salt, mix with the dongchimi brine and chill overnight until icy.
Cook the noodles in boiling water for 1–2 minutes (check the pack), rinse vigorously under cold water and drain into nests.

5 tbsp rice vinegar and 2 tbsp sugar (for curing the fish)
2 tbsp gochujang, 2 tbsp sugar, 2 tbsp grated pear

Hot beef broth (yuksu) to serve on the side
steps: Poach the fish slices in simmering water for 3 minutes until cooked through, cool, then marinate in the vinegar and sugar for 20 minutes and squeeze dry.
Mix the fish with half the gochugaru and a little sugar to make the fiery hoe-muchim topping.
Combine the remaining gochugaru, gochujang, sugar, pear, garlic and sesame oil into a sauce.

ingredients: 3 tbsp gochugaru, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp vinegar, 1 tbsp Korean mustard (for the dip)
steps: Simmer the chicken in 3 l water with the onion, leek and garlic for 40 minutes until cooked through; transfer to a wide hotpot with the broth.
Mix the gochugaru with a little hot broth, soy sauce, vinegar and mustard to make the Jongno-style dipping sauce, adding chives.

ingredients: 300 g split, skinned mung beans, soaked 6 hours
150 g pork mince or sliced pork belly
200 g mature napa cabbage kimchi, chopped
150 g mung bean sprouts, blanched and squeezed
2 cloves garlic, minced, and 1 tsp salt
2 tbsp glutinous rice flour (optional, for binding)
6 tbsp vegetable oil or pork fat for frying
steps: Drain the mung beans and blend with about 150 ml water to a coarse, thick batter.
Season the pork with garlic and a pinch of salt and mix into the batter with the kimchi, sprouts, spring onion, rice flour and salt.
Heat a generous layer of oil in a pan over medium heat, spoon in 12 cm pancakes 1 cm thick and fry 4–5 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp and the pork is cooked.

ingredients: 1 tbsp sesame oil and 1/2 tsp salt
150 g spinach, blanched and seasoned with sesame oil
200 g danmuji (yellow pickled radish), cut into thin sticks
2 sheets eomuk (fish cake), cut into strips and stir-fried
2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp water, 1 tsp Korean mustard (dipping sauce)
steps: Season the rice with sesame oil and salt.
Spread a thin layer of rice on each quarter sheet of gim, lay a strip each of carrot, spinach, radish and fish cake along one edge and roll tightly.

steps: Mix the gochugaru, gochujang, soy sauce and garlic into a seasoning paste.

Lettuce, perilla leaves and ssamjang to serve
steps: Score the meat and soak the ribs in cold water for 30 minutes to remove blood, then pat dry.
Rub with the salt, pear, garlic, sesame oil and pepper (Suwon's style is salt-seasoned rather than soy-marinated) and rest 30 minutes.
Grill over hot charcoal or on a grill plate, unrolling the long meat ribbon, for 4–5 minutes per side until well browned and cooked through.
Cut into pieces with scissors and serve with lettuce wraps, ssamjang and rice.

4 tbsp grated Korean pear or kiwi
1 tbsp sesame oil and 1/2 tsp black pepper
Lettuce, onion salad and ssamjang to serve
steps: Soak the ribs in cold water for 20 minutes, drain and pat dry.
Mix the soy sauce, sugar, pear, garlic, spring onion, sesame oil and pepper and marinate the ribs for at least 40 minutes.
Grill over medium-hot charcoal for 3–4 minutes per side until caramelised and cooked through.

200 g dried napa cabbage leaves (ugeoji), blanched
200 g sonji (coagulated ox blood), cubed, optional
3 tbsp gochugaru mixed with 1 tbsp sesame oil (chilli oil paste)
2 spring onions and 1 tsp perilla seed powder
steps: Scrub the tripe with flour and salt, rinse, blanch for 10 minutes and drain.
Simmer the tripe and brisket in the bone broth for 1.5 hours until tender, lift out and slice.
Add the doenjang, garlic, cabbage and sprouts to the broth and simmer 10 minutes; add the blood cubes (if using) and sliced meat and simmer 5 minutes more.

ingredients: 400 g jjolmyeon noodles (chewy wheat-starch noodles) or thick naengmyeon noodles
3 tbsp rice vinegar and 2 tbsp sugar
2 tbsp soy sauce and 2 cloves garlic minced
200 g bean sprouts and 100 g cabbage, shredded
1 tbsp sesame oil and 1 tsp sesame seeds
steps: Mix the gochujang, gochugaru, vinegar, sugar, soy sauce, garlic and sesame oil into a sauce and rest 10 minutes.
Blanch the bean sprouts for 2 minutes and cool.
Boil the noodles for 4–5 minutes until chewy, rinse hard under cold water and drain.
Top the noodles with cabbage, cucumber, carrot, sprouts, sauce and egg, sprinkle with sesame and toss well before eating.

ingredients: 800 g Manila clams (bajirak), purged in salted water for 1 hour
400 g fresh kalguksu noodles (or homemade with 300 g flour)
1 tbsp guk-ganjang and salt to taste
2 spring onions and 1 green chilli, sliced
steps: Scrub the purged clams and rinse well.
Bring the stock to a boil with the potato, add the noodles (shaking off excess flour) and cook 3 minutes.
Add the clams, zucchini and garlic and boil for 4–5 minutes until all clams open and the noodles are tender; discard any that stay closed.

ingredients: 1.5 kg Ganghwa sunmu (purple-topped turnips) with greens, or regular turnips
3 tbsp myeolchi-aekjeot (anchovy fish sauce) and 1 tbsp saeujeot (salted shrimp)
1 tbsp glutinous rice flour cooked with 200 ml water into a paste
6 cloves garlic and 1 thumb ginger, minced

Cool the rice paste and mix with the gochugaru, fish sauce, salted shrimp, garlic, ginger and sugar.
Toss the turnips and spring onions in the paste until evenly red and pack tightly into a jar.
Ferment at room temperature for 1 day, then refrigerate; it is ready in 3–4 days and develops its peppery, mustardy Ganghwa flavour over two weeks.

ingredients: 800 g boneless chicken thighs, cut into large bite-size pieces
2 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp curry powder
5 cloves garlic and 1 thumb ginger, minced
2 spring onions, cut 5 cm long, and 2 tbsp vegetable oil
steps: Mix the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar, curry powder, garlic and ginger and marinate the chicken for 30 minutes.

ingredients: 500 ml dongchimi (radish water kimchi) brine, chilled
300 ml cold beef or kelp broth
1 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp vinegar, 2 cloves garlic minced
1 tbsp sesame oil, 2 tbsp crushed toasted sesame seeds and crumbled gim
steps: Mix the gochujang, gochugaru, sugar, vinegar, garlic and sesame oil into a sauce; combine the dongchimi brine and broth and keep icy cold.
Boil the noodles for 4 minutes until just tender, then rinse vigorously in cold water and drain.
Place the noodles in bowls with the sauce, kimchi, cucumber, egg, sesame and gim.
Pour over some of the cold broth just before eating; Chuncheon diners add sugar, vinegar and mustard to taste.

ingredients: 400 ml clean seawater, or 1 tbsp nigari (magnesium chloride) dissolved in 300 ml water
3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp gochugaru, 1 spring onion chopped, 1 tsp sesame oil (yangnyeom-jang)
steps: Blend the soaked beans with the water until smooth, strain through a cloth bag and squeeze out all the soy milk.
Bring the soy milk to a boil in a large pot, stirring constantly so it does not scorch, then simmer 10 minutes.
Turn the heat to low, slowly pour in the seawater (the Chodang village method) or nigari solution and stir gently once; leave 15 minutes until soft curds form.
Ladle the warm curds with some whey into bowls and serve with the soy-chilli seasoning sauce, rice and kimchi.

ingredients: 1.2 l vegetable-kelp stock (dashima and dried shiitake)
1 spring onion, sliced, and 1 tbsp crumbled gim

Mix the pulp, starch and salt and roll into 3 cm balls (ongsimi).
Bring the stock to a boil with onion and garlic, add the dumplings and simmer for 6–8 minutes until they float and turn translucent.
Add the zucchini and soy sauce, cook 3 minutes more and serve with spring onion and gim.

ingredients: 1 green chilli and 1 red chilli, thinly sliced
2 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tbsp vinegar for dipping
steps: Grate the potatoes and onion finely (or blend), drain in a sieve for 5 minutes, and keep the starch that settles from the liquid.
Mix the pulp, starch and salt into a thick batter.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat, spread 10 cm rounds thinly, top with chilli and fry 3–4 minutes per side until crisp and golden.
Serve hot with soy-vinegar dipping sauce.

ingredients: 200 g cooked red kidney beans or sweetened red bean paste
steps: Mix the starch and salt and pour in the boiling water a little at a time, kneading into a smooth, firm dough.
Mix the beans with the sugar for the filling.
Take walnut-size pieces of dough, flatten, add a spoon of filling and close into half-moons, pressing with fingers to leave the traditional finger marks.
Steam over boiling water for 15–20 minutes until translucent grey, then brush with sesame oil while warm.

ingredients: 300 g plain flour, 150 ml water, 1/2 tsp salt
1 tbsp guk-ganjang and salt to taste
2 spring onions and 1 green chilli, sliced
steps: Knead the flour, water and salt into a soft dough, cover and rest in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Bring the stock to a boil with the potatoes and onion and cook 5 minutes.
Wet your hands, stretch the dough very thin and tear bite-size pieces straight into the boiling soup, then cook 5 minutes until the pieces float.
Add zucchini, garlic and soup soy sauce, cook 3 minutes and finish with spring onion and chilli.

ingredients: 200 g buckwheat flour and 400 ml water, pinch of salt
300 g cabbage kimchi, finely chopped and squeezed
50 g dangmyeon (glass noodles), soaked and chopped
1 tbsp sesame oil, 2 cloves garlic minced
steps: Stir-fry the pork with garlic over medium-high heat for 4 minutes until cooked, then mix with the kimchi, tofu, noodles, spring onion and sesame oil.
Whisk the buckwheat flour, water and salt into a thin batter.
Lightly oil a pan over medium heat and pour a thin 18 cm round, cooking for 1 minute until set.

ingredients: 8 large napa cabbage leaves, lightly salted
50 g pork belly, thinly sliced (optional topping)
4 tbsp perilla oil or vegetable oil

Heat oil in a pan over medium heat, lay cabbage leaves, kimchi leaves, pork slices and spring onion flat in a single layer.

ingredients: 300 g buckwheat flour and 100 g wheat flour
1 tbsp gochugaru and 1 tbsp sesame oil

Roll thin, cut into thick noodles (the short, brittle buckwheat strands give the dish its name, 'hit like a flower').

ingredients: 400 g short-grain rice, washed and soaked 30 minutes
100 g dried gondeure (Korean thistle), soaked overnight or 200 g fresh; substitute dried chard or chwinamul
4 tbsp soy sauce, 1 spring onion minced, 1 tsp gochugaru, 1 tbsp sesame oil, 1 tsp sesame seeds (yangnyeom-jang)
steps: Boil the soaked gondeure for 20 minutes, rinse, squeeze and cut into 3 cm pieces (count this with the cook time if dried).
Toss the gondeure with the perilla oil and soup soy sauce.
Put the drained rice in a heavy pot, spread the gondeure on top, add the water, bring to a boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes; rest 10 minutes.
Fluff and serve with the seasoned soy sauce to mix in, a Jeongseon and Pyeongchang mountain specialty.

ingredients: 200 g fine cornmeal or corn flour and 100 g plain flour
200 ml warm water and 1/2 tsp salt
2 cloves garlic, minced, and 1 tbsp guk-ganjang
steps: Mix the corn and wheat flours, salt and warm water into a soft dough and rest 20 minutes.
Simmer the potatoes and onion in the stock for 5 minutes.
Tear flattened bite-size pieces of dough into the boiling soup and cook 6–7 minutes until cooked through.
Add the zucchini, garlic and soup soy sauce for 3 minutes and serve with spring onion.

ingredients: 4 medium squid, cleaned with tentacles reserved
200 g firm tofu, squeezed and mashed
50 g dangmyeon (glass noodles), soaked and chopped
2 eggs, beaten, plus 1 extra for coating
2 cloves garlic, minced, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp pepper
2 tbsp potato starch and 3 tbsp vegetable oil
steps: Chop the tentacles and mix with the tofu, pork, vegetables, noodles, 2 eggs, garlic, salt and pepper.
Dust the inside of each squid tube with starch, pack with the filling (not too tight) and seal the opening with a toothpick.
Steam over boiling water for 20 minutes until the filling is cooked through, then cool slightly.
Slice into 2 cm rounds, dip in beaten egg and pan-fry 1 minute per side; serve with soy-vinegar sauce, as at Sokcho's Abai village.

ingredients: 1 m cleaned pork large intestine casing (or large hog casing)
200 g soybean sprouts, blanched and chopped
3 cloves garlic, 1 tbsp doenjang, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp pepper
2 tbsp perilla seed powder and 2 spring onions, chopped
steps: Rinse the casing inside and out with salt and flour, then rinse well.
Mix the pork, rice, sprouts, cabbage, blood (if using), garlic, doenjang, salt, pepper, perilla powder and spring onion.
Tie one end of the casing and stuff loosely, tying the other end; prick a few holes.

Simmer in barely bubbling water for 40 minutes, then steam 15 minutes until the filling reaches 75°C; slice thick and serve with salt-pepper dip and salted shrimp, as the North Korean refugees of Abai village made it.

ingredients: 2 whole hwangtae (winter-dried yellow pollock), split; substitute bugeo (dried pollock)
1 tbsp rice syrup or honey, 1 tbsp sugar
1 tbsp sesame oil and 1 tsp sesame seeds
steps: Soak the pollock in water for 20 minutes, squeeze, remove fins and bones, and score the skin side to stop curling.
Brush with a mix of soy sauce and sesame oil and pre-grill or pan-fry over medium heat for 3 minutes per side.
Mix the gochujang, gochugaru, syrup, sugar and garlic, spread over the fish and grill 2 minutes more per side over low heat until glossy.
Sprinkle with sesame and serve with rice; Inje and Yongdae-ri in Gangwon are famous for this.

ingredients: 60 g shredded hwangtae or bugeo (dried pollock)
1 tbsp saeujeot (salted shrimp) or salt, 1 tbsp guk-ganjang
2 spring onions and 1 green chilli, sliced
steps: Soak the pollock briefly, squeeze and season with a little soup soy sauce.
Stir-fry the pollock and radish in the sesame oil over medium heat for 3 minutes until fragrant, then add the water and boil 10 minutes until milky.
Add the sprouts and garlic and boil 5 minutes with the lid on.
Season with salted shrimp, drizzle in the egg, add spring onion and chilli, and serve with rice.

ingredients: 1 kg small flounder (gajami), cleaned, heads and fins removed, cut into strips
6 cloves garlic and 1 thumb ginger, minced

2 tbsp malt powder (yeotgireum) or 1 tbsp sugar
steps: Salt the pollock strips and refrigerate for 1 day, then squeeze out the moisture.
Salt the radish for 1 hour, squeeze dry and colour it with half the gochugaru.
Mix the pollock, radish, millet, remaining gochugaru, garlic, ginger, malt and fish sauce and pack into a jar.

Simmer the syrup, gochujang, ketchup, soy sauce, sugar, chillies and sliced garlic over low heat for 3 minutes until glossy.

1 onion, 1 apple, 10 cloves garlic, 1 thumb ginger
10 x 10 cm dashima (kelp) and 5 dried shiitake

4 cloves garlic, minced, and 1 tsp grated ginger

Mix the radish with gochugaru until red, then add fish sauce, garlic, ginger, sugar and spring onion.

300 g fresh oysters, shucked and rinsed in salted water
4 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and sliced

Mix the soy sauce, gochugaru, spring onion, sesame oil, seeds and chives, and serve the rice with the sauce to stir in.

ingredients: 1.5 m cleaned pork small intestine casings
200 g soybean sprouts, blanched and chopped

1 tbsp guk-ganjang and salt to taste

ingredients: 300 g olgaengi (freshwater marsh snails), live in shell, or 150 g cooked snail meat

ingredients: 1 kg beef brisket and shank (yangjimeori and satae)
500 g beef bones, soaked in cold water 1 hour to remove blood
1 whole head garlic, plus 3 cloves minced

Strain the broth, season with soup soy sauce and salt, and keep boiling.

300 g siraegi (dried radish greens), soaked and boiled until soft
2 spring onions, sliced, plus 1 tsp chopi powder (Korean prickly ash, substitute Sichuan pepper)
